final_decision.rationale: Single deterministic isotropic blur: gm_ratio=0.649/0.519/0.571 (pairs 0/1/2), spectral_slope_ratio 1.04-1.06, block_boundary 1.012/1.001/0.981 (no JPEG, 0%FP signal), noise_prior sigma 0.74/1.11/0.74 <2 (NO_NOISE), global stats near-identity (mean_shift -0.5/-0.5/-0.4, variance_ratio 0.945/0.949/0.991, chroma 0.972/0.977/0.992). Among all tested families (gaussian sev1-5, lens sev1-3, glass 2, motion 1-2, jpeg 1/2/4, blur+jpeg, identity control 23.45dB) gaussian sev2 is best on all three pairs. Verdict stays UNCERTAIN: PSNR 25.7-32.6dB is below the 40dB LIKELY threshold and Wiener kernel corr=0.718<0.9, i.e., the exact PSF is not reproduced by any legal integer severity; residual is structured (spatial_corr 0.98, std 13.2) yet non-random. The run_full_analysis BLUR_UNLIKELY verdict is a false negative caused by the blur-induced YCrCb noise FP forcing the spectral-slope branch (slope_ratio 1.057 just below 1.08); gm_ratio is meaningful here and indicates blur. Budget hit the 25-test hard cap; no further deterministic hypothesis (global steps are excluded by first-order stats; additive noise excluded by wavelet sigma) remains within x_distortion's discrete severities.

reflection_R1.rationale: R1 reanalysis confirms a single mild isotropic blur. Simulation inversion is the decisive new signal: gaussian:2 slightly over-blurs and the target sits between sev1 and sev2, but no legal x_distortion blur reproduces the target PSF (k=3 PSNR 24.3-32.6 dB across 5 newly validated candidates), and global/quantization/noise steps are quantitatively excluded. No candidate gains +2 dB or reaches 40 dB, so the R0 pipeline is retained item-by-item; lens:2 is statistically tied with better CI and becomes the primary cross-family alternative.
